name: core
description: The workflow core: triage, operate, post-op, peer-review, ship and the supporting commands, rules, hooks and Claude/Codex sync. Always installed.

facts.name: PROJECT_NAME
facts.meaning: Short name, used in reports and notifications
facts.ask: What short name should reports and notifications use for this project?

facts.name: PROJECT_SUMMARY
facts.meaning: One line on what the product does
facts.ask: In one line, what does this product do?

facts.name: TICKET_SYSTEM
facts.meaning: The installed ticket pack
facts.ask: Which ticket system does this project use? (v1 supports jira)

facts.name: TICKET_PREFIX
facts.meaning: Ticket key prefix (keys look like ABC-123)
facts.ask: What is the ticket key prefix (the ABC in ABC-123)?

facts.name: MCP_PREFIX
facts.meaning: Prefix on this project's MCP server names, so tools from different projects never mix
facts.ask: What prefix should this project's MCP server names get? Use the project's short name and an underscore (acme_ makes acme_jira, acme_supabase), so one project's agent never calls another project's Jira or database. Lowercase letters, digits and _ only; answer none for no prefix.

facts.name: MAIN_BRANCH
facts.meaning: The only long-lived branch
facts.ask: What is the main branch called? The kit assumes it is the only long-lived branch.

facts.name: BRANCH_PREFIX
facts.meaning: Feature branch prefix
facts.ask: What prefix should feature branches use?

facts.name: HAS_CI
facts.meaning: true means /ship waits for required checks before merging
facts.ask: Does this repo have CI checks that must pass before a merge (true/false)?

facts.name: TEST_COMMANDS
facts.meaning: One line per package, '<dir>: <command>'. Run exactly as written
facts.ask: Which command runs the full test suite, per package? One '<dir>: <command>' line each.

facts.name: TYPECHECK_COMMAND
facts.meaning: Type check command, or none
facts.ask: Which command type-checks the code, if any?

facts.name: BUILD_COMMAND
facts.meaning: Build check command, or none
facts.ask: Which command builds the project, if any?

facts.name: SYNTAX_CHECK_COMMAND
facts.meaning: Syntax check for code with no compiler, or none
facts.ask: Is there a syntax-check command for uncompiled code (e.g. node --check)?

facts.name: DEV_SERVER_COMMAND
facts.meaning: How /verify runs the app locally
facts.ask: How do you run the app locally?

facts.name: LOG_SINK
facts.meaning: Where production logs are read, or none
facts.ask: Where are production logs read?

facts.name: CRITICAL_DOMAIN
facts.meaning: Severity class S3: a label plus one line on the logic that must never be wrong here
facts.ask: What is the one area of logic that must never be wrong in this project? Give a label and one line.

facts.name: CRITICAL_SYSTEMS
facts.meaning: Areas whose changes get the stricter Critical Systems checks
facts.ask: Which areas should get the stricter Critical Systems checks?

facts.name: OWNER_KEPT_GATES
facts.meaning: Extra owner-kept gates on top of G1-G7, or none
facts.ask: Besides the seven default gates, is there anything else an agent must never do without your yes?

facts.name: OPEN_ITEMS_TICKET
facts.meaning: The standing tracker ticket key for noted findings
facts.ask: Which ticket should collect noted (non-blocking) findings? The agent can create one.

facts.name: CO_AUTHOR_TRAILER
facts.meaning: Commit trailer line, or none
facts.ask: Should commits carry a co-author trailer line? Give it, or none.

facts.name: UI_LANGUAGE
facts.meaning: Language of user-facing copy
facts.ask: What language is the user-facing copy in?

facts.name: SYNTHETIC_MARKER
facts.meaning: Column or flag on rows that /verify creates
facts.ask: Which column or flag marks rows that /verify creates (operator screens filter it out)?

facts.name: DEPENDENCY_POLICY
facts.meaning: When a new dependency is allowed
facts.example: allowed when it's the right tool; say why in the PR
facts.default: allowed when it's the right tool; say why in the PR
facts.ask: When is adding a new dependency allowed?
